examples.ko: 운동을 꾸준히 하면 다이어트 효과가 배가해요.
examples.en: If you exercise steadily, the diet effect doubles.
Thanks to my friends' cheering, my joy doubled.

examples.ko: 가격이 오르면 부담도 배가하는 것 같아요.
examples.en: If prices go up, the burden seems to grow twofold too.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 공부 효과를 배가해 줘요.
examples.en: This app multiplies the effect of your studying.

examples.ko: 노력을 배가하면 좋은 결과가 나올 거예요.
examples.en: If you redouble your effort, you will get good results.
The hot weather doubled the feeling of fatigue.

explain: 주로 노력, 효과, 기쁨, 재미, 부담처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에 써요. 말할 때는 '두 배로 늘다, 훨씬 커지다'라고 많이 하고, '배가하다'는 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 보여요. 몸의 '배'(belly)와는 관계없고, 여기서 '배'는 '두 배'의 배예요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for things you cannot see, such as effort, effects, joy, fun or burden. In speech people often say '두 배로 늘다' or '훨씬 커지다', while '배가하다' shows up more in news and writing. It has nothing to do with 배 (belly); here 배 is the one in '두 배' (twofold).

examples.en: I reject prejudice and discrimination.

examples.ko: 새로운 의견을 무조건 배격하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't reject new opinions outright.
The chairman rejected that outdated way of doing things.

examples.ko: 사람들은 거짓말과 속임수를 배격하는 문화를 원해요.
examples.en: People want a culture that rejects lies and tricks.

examples.ko: 그는 다른 문화를 배격하지 않고 늘 열린 태도를 보여요.
examples.en: He doesn't shut out other cultures and always shows an open attitude.

examples.ko: 이 단체는 어떤 차별도 배격한다고 밝혔어요.
examples.en: This organization stated that it rejects any kind of discrimination.

explain: '거부하다'보다 훨씬 강하고 딱딱해요. 어떤 생각, 태도, 방식을 아예 받아들이지 않겠다는 입장을 말할 때 주로 쓰고, 사람에게 쓰는 일은 드물어요. 일상 대화에서는 '안 받아들이다, 거부하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is much stronger and stiffer than '거부하다' (to refuse). It is mainly used for taking a stand against an idea, attitude or method, and rarely for people. In daily talk people say '안 받아들이다' or '거부하다'.

examples.en: What is this car's engine displacement?
The bigger the displacement, the higher the car tax.

examples.ko: 제 오토바이는 배기량이 작아서 연비가 좋아요.
examples.en: My motorcycle has a small displacement, so its fuel economy is good.
I want to buy a 2000cc car.

examples.ko: 요즘은 배기량이 작은 차도 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: These days small-displacement cars are popular too.

examples.ko: 작은 배기량에 비해 힘이 좋아서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised at how powerful it is for such a small displacement.

explain: 자동차나 오토바이 엔진의 크기를 말할 때 써요. 보통 'cc'로 말하고, '2000cc급'처럼 '~급'을 붙이기도 해요. 자동차세나 보험 이야기에서도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used for the size of a car or motorcycle engine, usually given in cc, and sometimes with '~급' as in '2000cc급'. It also comes up often when talking about car tax or insurance.

examples.en: I bought a newborn's jacket before the baby was born.

examples.ko: 엄마가 제 배냇저고리를 아직 보관하고 있어요.
examples.en: My mom still keeps my baby jacket.

examples.ko: 병원에서 갓 태어난 아기에게 배냇저고리를 입혀 줬어요.
examples.en: At the hospital they dressed the newborn baby in a baenaet-jeogori (first jacket).

examples.ko: 배냇저고리는 보통 흰색이나 연한 색이 많아요.
examples.en: Baenaet jackets are usually white or light colors.
My friend gave me a pretty baby jacket as a gift.
The newborn jacket was so tiny that it amazed me.

explain: 갓 태어난 아기에게 처음 입히는 작은 저고리예요. 아기 옷 전체를 말하는 게 아니라 이 옷만 가리켜요. 출산 준비물이나 육아 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the small jacket put on a baby right after birth. It refers only to this garment, not to baby clothes in general. It often comes up when talking about birth preparations or child care.

examples.en: It rained a lot, so the drainage ditch got blocked.
The villagers cleaned the drainage ditch together.

examples.ko: 도로 옆 배수로에 낙엽이 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: Fallen leaves are piled up in the ditch beside the road.

examples.ko: 장마 전에 배수로를 새로 만들기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to build a new drainage channel before the rainy season.
Thanks to the drainage channel, the water drains well.
We need to dig a drainage ditch beside the field.

explain: 물이 잘 빠져나가도록 만든 길이에요. 장마나 큰비 이야기에서 '배수로가 막히다, 배수로를 정비하다'처럼 자주 써요. 하수구보다 길게 파 놓은 도랑 같은 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is a channel built so water can drain away, and it comes up often in talk of the rainy season or heavy rain, as in '배수로가 막히다' or '배수로를 정비하다'. Compared with a 하수구 (drain), it feels more like a long ditch dug in the ground.

examples.en: I studied with my back against the wall for this exam.

examples.ko: 그는 배수진을 친 각오로 사업을 시작했어요.
examples.en: He started the business with a do-or-die resolve.

examples.ko: 배수진을 치지 않으면 끝까지 하기 어려워요.
examples.en: If you don't cut off your own retreat, it's hard to see it through.
I heard they came out with their backs against the wall in this game.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 배수진을 친 만큼 포기하지 않을 거예요.
examples.en: Since our team has no way back, we won't give up.
I staked my severance pay and went all in.

explain: 거의 항상 '배수진을 치다'로 써요. 물러설 곳이 없다는 각오로 끝까지 해 보겠다는 뜻으로, 시험, 경기, 사업 이야기에 잘 어울려요. 원래 전쟁에서 나온 말이지만 지금은 일상에서 비유로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I went all in to pass this exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물러설 곳을 없애고 죽을 각오로 일에 임한다는 비유예요. 시험, 경기, 사업 같은 큰일에 잘 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for cutting off any retreat and committing completely. It suits big matters such as exams, games and business.
phrases.en_equiv: put one's back against the wall; burn one's boats

explain_en: It is almost always used as '배수진을 치다'. It expresses a resolve to see things through with no way back, and fits talk of exams, games and business. It began as a military term, but today it is mostly used figuratively in daily life.

examples.en: The child saw me and gave a shy little smile.
She gave a little smile when she heard the compliment.
My younger sibling just smiled faintly without saying anything.

examples.ko: 그는 쑥스러운지 배시시 웃으며 고개를 숙였어요.
examples.en: He seemed embarrassed and bowed his head with a faint smile.

examples.ko: 아기가 배시시 웃는 모습이 너무 귀여워요.
examples.en: The way the baby smiles softly is so cute.

examples.ko: 뭐가 좋은지 하루 종일 배시시 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: For some reason she's been smiling to herself all day.

explain: '웃다'와 거의 같이 쓰이고, 소리 없이 입가만 살짝 웃는 모습을 그려요. 쑥스럽거나 기분이 좋을 때 어울리고, 큰 소리로 웃는 것에는 쓰지 않아요. 아이나 가까운 사람을 이야기할 때 귀엽고 다정한 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It almost always goes with '웃다' and pictures a soundless, slight smile at the corners of the mouth. It fits shy or happy moments, and not loud laughter. When talking about children or people close to you, it carries a cute, warm feel.

examples.en: The lunch duty students serve the lunch.
Volunteers served warm meals for free.

examples.ko: 학교에서는 아이들이 줄을 서면 선생님이 배식하세요.
examples.en: At school, when the kids line up, the teacher serves the food.
Today is my day to serve the food.
Serving time at the cafeteria starts at twelve.

examples.ko: 다 같이 줄을 서서 순서대로 배식했어요.
examples.en: We all lined up and got served in order.

explain: 급식, 무료 급식, 군대 식당처럼 많은 사람에게 음식을 차례로 나눠 줄 때 써요. 식당에서 손님에게 음식을 가져다주는 것에는 '서빙하다'나 '내오다'가 어울려요. 음식을 받는 쪽은 '배식을 받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when food is handed out in turn to many people, such as school meals, free meals or a barracks mess hall. For bringing food to customers in a restaurant, '서빙하다' or '내오다' fits better. The person receiving food says '배식을 받다'.

examples.en: Sweat started to seep out on my forehead.
The writer's sadness comes through in that piece.
Tiredness came through in his voice.
Sweat has soaked through my clothes, so I feel uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 그의 말투에서 정이 배어나는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I feel warmth coming through in the way he speaks.

examples.ko: 손바닥에 땀이 배어나서 긴장한 게 티가 났어요.
examples.en: Sweat seeped out on my palms, so it was obvious I was nervous.

explain: 속에 있던 것이 겉으로 스며 나온다는 느낌이에요. 땀처럼 눈에 보이는 것에도 쓰고, 슬픔이나 정처럼 말투나 글에서 느껴지는 감정에도 써요. 비슷한 '묻어나다'는 손이나 옷에 묻는 것에도 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It gives the feel of something inside seeping out to the surface. It is used for visible things like sweat and also for feelings such as sadness or warmth that you sense in someone's speech or writing. The similar '묻어나다' can also be used for something that rubs off onto hands or clothes.

examples.en: The smell of grilled meat soaked into my clothes.

examples.ko: 양념이 속까지 배어들게 한 시간 재워 두세요.
examples.en: Let it marinate for an hour so the seasoning soaks all the way in.

examples.ko: 찌개 냄새가 커튼에 배어들어서 빨아야 해요.
examples.en: The stew smell has soaked into the curtains, so I have to wash them.
The long-time habit has sunk into my body.

examples.ko: 국물에 맛이 배어들 때까지 끓여 주세요.
examples.en: Please boil it until the flavor soaks into the broth.
I changed before the sweat soaked into my shirt.

explain: 냄새, 양념, 땀 같은 것이 안으로 깊이 스며드는 것을 말해요. 습관이나 버릇이 몸에 익는다는 뜻으로는 보통 '몸에 배다'라고 해요. '배어나다'가 밖으로 나오는 것이라면 '배어들다'는 안으로 들어가는 거예요.
explain_en: It describes smells, seasoning or sweat soaking deep into something. For a habit becoming ingrained, people usually say '몸에 배다'. If '배어나다' is something coming out, '배어들다' is something going in.

examples.ko: 현미경 배율을 높이면 더 자세히 보여요.
examples.en: If you raise the microscope's magnification, you can see in more detail.
What is the magnification of this telescope?
The higher the magnification, the narrower the field of view.
I adjusted the magnification when enlarging the photo.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 배율이 다른 렌즈를 비교했어요.
examples.en: In science class we compared lenses with different magnifications.

examples.ko: 쌍안경은 배율이 열 배 정도면 충분해요.
examples.en: For binoculars, around ten times magnification is enough.

explain: 현미경, 망원경, 카메라 렌즈처럼 크게 보이게 하는 도구에서 얼마나 크게 보이는지를 말해요. '배율이 높다/낮다', '배율을 조절하다'처럼 자주 써요. '해상도'는 얼마나 선명한지를 말하니까 달라요.
explain_en: It tells how much larger something looks through tools such as microscopes, telescopes and camera lenses. It is used in phrases like '배율이 높다/낮다' and '배율을 조절하다'. It differs from '해상도' (resolution), which is about how sharp the image is.

examples.en: Ignoring the person who helped you is just ingratitude.
I think that's an ungrateful thing to do.
Forgetting a favor is really ungrateful.
It's ungrateful to treat your parents like that after they raised you.

examples.ko: 그 친구의 배은망덕한 행동에 크게 실망했어요.
examples.en: I was very disappointed by that friend's ungrateful behavior.
I'm worried people will call me ungrateful.

explain: 도움이나 은혜를 받고도 고마워하지 않거나 오히려 해를 끼치는 사람을 비난할 때 써요. 꽤 강한 말이라서 가까운 사이에서 가볍게 쓰면 심하게 들릴 수 있어요. 보통 '배은망덕하다', '배은망덕한 사람'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is used to criticize someone who received help or a favor and showed no gratitude, or even did harm in return. It is a fairly strong word, so using it lightly with close friends can sound harsh. It is usually used as '배은망덕하다' or '배은망덕한 사람'.

examples.en: I chose my seat after looking at the office layout.
The exam room seating chart is posted on the door.

examples.ko: 가구 배치도를 그려서 이사 준비를 했어요.
examples.en: I drew a furniture layout to prepare for the move.

examples.ko: 전시장 배치도를 보면 길을 쉽게 찾을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you look at the exhibition hall layout, you can find your way easily.
Where is the restroom on the building's layout?

examples.ko: 새 교실 배치도를 선생님께 보여 드렸어요.
examples.en: I showed the new classroom layout to the teacher.

explain: 사람, 가구, 건물이 어디에 놓이는지 보여 주는 그림이나 표예요. 시험장 자리, 사무실, 이사, 행사장 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 건물 안의 방 구조를 그린 '평면도'와 비슷하지만, '배치도'는 무엇이 어디에 놓이는지에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It is a drawing or chart showing where people, furniture or buildings are placed, and it comes up often with exam seating, offices, moving and event venues. It is similar to a '평면도' (floor plan), but '배치도' focuses on what is placed where.

en: no matter how long; for ages

examples.ko: 백날 말해도 그 사람은 안 들어요.
examples.en: No matter how long you tell him, he won't listen.

examples.ko: 백날 연습만 하면 뭐 해요, 실전에서 못 하면요.
examples.en: What's the use of practicing forever if you can't do it in the real thing?

examples.ko: 백날 기다려 봐야 연락은 안 올 거예요.
examples.en: You can wait all you want, but no call will come.
Crying like that for ages won't help at all.

examples.ko: 백날 부탁해 봐야 안 된다고 할 거예요.
examples.en: No matter how often you ask, they'll say no.

examples.ko: 이렇게 앉아만 있으면 백날 해도 안 끝나요.
examples.en: If you just sit here like this, it won't be finished no matter how long you go on.

explain: 실제로 백 일을 말하는 게 아니라 '아무리 오래 해도'라는 느낌으로 써요. 뒤에 '~어도, ~아 봐야'와 함께 안 된다, 소용없다는 말이 오는 때가 많아요. 불만이나 답답함을 나타내는 구어 표현이에요.
explain_en: It does not literally mean a hundred days; it carries the feel of 'no matter how long you do it'. It often comes with '~어도' or '~아 봐야' followed by a negative result such as 'it won't work' or 'it's useless'. It is a spoken expression that conveys frustration or exasperation.

examples.en: My grandmother had cataract surgery.
Cataracts are easy to develop as you get older.
I heard things look hazy because of cataracts.

examples.ko: 아버지는 백내장 검사를 받으러 병원에 가셨어요.
examples.en: My father went to the hospital for a cataract exam.
Cataracts are easier to treat if found early.
My eyes felt dim, so I worried it might be cataracts.

explain: '백내장 수술', '백내장에 걸리다'처럼 써요. 소리가 비슷한 '녹내장'은 시신경이 상하는 다른 병이니까 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It is used in phrases like '백내장 수술' (cataract surgery) and '백내장에 걸리다'. Don't mix it up with '녹내장' (glaucoma), which sounds similar but is a different condition that damages the optic nerve.
